sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Celina
sections.html:
A direct cash sale is usually the quickest Celina route, since nobody waits on a buyer's loan or a repair list. Slower routes may bring a better price for a house in strong shape.

  • An agent suits a house that shows well and a seller who can wait for lender approval.
  • A sale by owner suits someone comfortable writing the contract and screening buyers.
  • A direct cash sale suits a house needing work, one with a tenant, an estate property, or a date you can't move.

sections.h2: Where Celina sits and why dates matter
sections.html:
Celina lies in northwestern Collin County on State Highway 289 and Farm Road 455, about fifteen miles northwest of McKinney and twelve miles north of Frisco. It was established in 1879, named by a settler for his native Celina, Tennessee, and incorporated in 1907. The city now describes rapid growth that it wants to balance with the town's heritage.

With that much change, check the date on any survey, plat or permit. A document from a decade ago may describe a very different lot, street or utility layout.

Celina's Building Services Division requires a permit to erect, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert, move or demolish any structure inside the city limits. Residential permits go through the residential permit desk at (945) 362-9250 or permits@celina-tx.gov, at 112 N. Colorado St.

Celina residential permit rules

If you pulled a permit for a pool, a garage conversion or a roof and never closed it, call the permit desk before you list. An unfinished permit can delay a title company even when the work looks complete. The city also publishes policy sheets on residential fences, the irrigation ordinance, wood structure columns and brace shear wall fasteners, so ask which apply if you built or changed any of those.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district values my Celina house?
sections.html:
Collin County houses are valued by the Collin Central Appraisal District. It has a page on a homestead exemption audit tied to Senate Bill 1801 and links to a tax transparency site where an owner can see the taxing units on a bill. A Celina address near a county line may sit on a different roll, so read the district named on your own statement. Then check the exemptions on the account, the value history and the units listed.

The state rules behind every Texas bill are short. Taxes are due on receipt in October and delinquent after January 31, and the year's lien attaches on January 1. Penalties start at six percent plus one percent interest the first month. Unpaid taxes show up in the buyer's title review, so ask your title company how the year's bill will be handled.

The school homestead exemption is $140,000. Older or disabled owners get an added school exemption and a tax ceiling, and disabled veterans receive bracketed exemptions. The district's site links to its homestead information and its appraisal review board.

A homestead exemption belongs to the person who lives in the house, so a buyer applies for their own. Have your current exemptions in front of you when you talk about taxes, so the buyer knows what the bill looked like under your ownership.

Texas attaches different clocks to each of these.

  • Inheritance: a will can be probated within four years of death. A small estate affidavit fits only when assets, apart from homestead and exempt property, come to $75,000 or less. An affidavit of heirship is sworn and filed with the clerk, but no law forces anyone to accept it.
  • Tenants: a landlord gives 3 days of written notice unless the lease differs, then files in justice court, where the hearing lands 10 to 21 days after filing.
  • Foreclosure: a borrower can reinstate during the 20 days after receiving the default notice, and courthouse sales happen on first Tuesdays.

Speak with a Texas attorney or the county clerk before signing a contract, and tell the buyer up front.

sections.h2: Papers to collect before asking for offers
sections.html:
A short folder saves days at closing.

  • The most recent tax statement and the appraisal district account number.
  • Any open permit number, and the final inspection record for finished work.
  • The mortgage payoff figure, if there is a loan.
  • Any HOA contact and dues balance.
  • Lease copies, if a tenant lives in the house.

faqs.q: How long does a Celina building permit stay valid?
faqs.a: It expires on the 181st day if no inspection has taken place or no progress has been shown. An application with no permit issued within 180 days is treated as abandoned. Call the residential permit desk at (945) 362-9250 for an exact status.

faqs.q: Do Celina homeowners pay a city tax separate from the county?
faqs.a: Texas has no state property tax, and each local unit that taxes your address sets its own rate. Your tax statement lists every unit. Call the tax office for rates before you estimate anything.

faqs.q: Is Celina in Collin County or Denton County?
faqs.a: Celina sits in northwestern Collin County, and the Collin Central Appraisal District values property there. Your own tax statement names the district that carries your parcel.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell a Celina house without full probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A muniment of title or small estate affidavit can work when the estate qualifies and the court approves. A probate attorney can confirm which fits.

faqs.q: Do repairs have to be finished before a Celina sale?
faqs.a: No. Many buyers purchase as-is. The main issue is an open permit, which you should disclose and, if possible, resolve with the city's permit desk first.
